correct_answer: The change order is NOT validly approved because the delegation memo was project-specific to Wacker Drive, not Lincoln Square, and email delegation does not meet the capital policy's Exhibit C requirement — the CO requires formal VP-level written approval before the work can proceed or payment can be released.
rationale: The delegation memo from Kowalski explicitly states 'This is for Wacker only' and instructs Webb to loop him in on anything over $50K on other jobs. Additionally, Section 4.3 of the Capital Expenditure Policy v3.2 requires delegation via the standard delegation form (Exhibit C) and explicitly states email delegation is not recognized — so even if the memo had referenced Lincoln Square, it would not meet policy requirements. The AIA contract independently requires written owner approval for COs over $50K. Answer B is wrong because an emoji reaction on Teams does not constitute 'written approval' under either the contract or the capital policy, and even if it did, the work was already approved and potentially commenced before this reaction. Answer C misreads the delegation as a blanket authority when the memo explicitly limits it to Wacker Drive. Answer D confuses contingency usage with change order validity — whether contingency funds cover the cost is a budget allocation question, not an approval authority question; the structural work is legitimately unforeseen and properly categorized as a CO.
